title: Scanning and locating specific information
blurb: Find the exact detail a question asks for: scan with key words, use headings and match every qualifier.
question: A clinic leaflet lists weekday hours at the library and Saturday hours at the high school gym. A question asks where to go for a flu shot on Saturday, and one answer choice names the library. How do you find the right detail fast, and why is the library a trap?

teach.h: Locating is a search, not a read
teach.body: Formally, locating specific information means finding a stated detail (a name, number, date, place or term) in a text and reporting it with the correct qualifiers. The skill is scanning: searching quickly for a particular word or number. In plain English: you are not reading the passage to understand it all; you are hunting for one fact, then checking it answers the exact question asked.

rows.label: Look for
values: A key word, number or name

teach.caption: Both are fast. Scanning stops when the target is found; skimming covers the whole text lightly.

teach.h: Text features that speed up the search
head: Feature
What it tells you
rows: Extra facts beside the main text

teach.body:
Lakeside Community Flu Clinic
Who can attend: Anyone 6 months or older. Children under 18 must come with a parent or guardian.
When and where: Weekdays, 4 to 7 p.m., Lakeside Library. Saturdays, 9 a.m. to 1 p.m., Lakeside High School gym.
What to bring: A photo ID and your insurance card. No insurance? Shots are free.
After your shot: Please wait 15 minutes before leaving.

teach.h: Five moves to the right detail
items: Underline the target in the question (Where?) and its qualifier (on a Saturday).
Choose the heading most likely to hold it: 'When and where'.
Scan that section for the qualifier word: 'Saturdays'.
Read the whole sentence around it: '9 a.m. to 1 p.m., Lakeside High School gym'.
Check the option against the qualifier, not just the topic: the gym, not the library.

steps.label: Scan
steps.sub: Find the word or a synonym

teach.body: Most wrong options in locate items are real details from the passage. They fail because they answer a slightly different question: weekday instead of Saturday, the old figure instead of the current one, children instead of adults, length instead of depth. Questions also paraphrase: the passage says 'homebound seniors', the question says 'older residents who cannot leave their homes'. Scan for meaning, not just the identical word.

teach.h: Why real details are wrong answers

children.label: Weekday hours for a Saturday question
The figure before a later change

teach.text: Watch for: a detail from the wrong section, row or paragraph; a number that was later updated ('...in 2023, two rooms became a lab'); a related but different item; and information that appears in the text but answers a different question. Finding the topic word is not the finish line: the qualifier is.

teach.body: Marcus Bell, applying to a surgical technology program, reads a passage saying a clinic opened with three exam rooms, moved to a building with eleven, and later converted two into a lab. Asked how many exam rooms it has today, he nearly picks 11, the figure for the new building. He reads on, sees the 2023 change and answers 9.

items: Scan for a specific word, number or name; skim for the general idea.
Use headings, bold words, lists and captions to find the right section.
Read the whole sentence around the match, and a little beyond.
Match every qualifier: day, group, date, unit, current vs past.
Most wrong options are real details that answer a different question.

summary: You can now locate specific details quickly by scanning for key words and synonyms and using headings and other text features. You can also confirm every qualifier so that a real but wrong detail does not catch you.

A.q:
Read the leaflet.

Lakeside Community Flu Clinic
Who can attend: Anyone 6 months or older. Children under 18 must come with a parent or guardian.
When and where: Weekdays, 4 to 7 p.m., Lakeside Library. Saturdays, 9 a.m. to 1 p.m., Lakeside High School gym.
What to bring: A photo ID and your insurance card. No insurance? Shots are free.

According to the leaflet, where should a person go for a flu shot on a Saturday?
A.why: Under 'When and where', the Saturday entry gives 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. at the Lakeside High School gym.

whyNot.1: The library is the weekday location, not the Saturday one.
whyNot.2: This is part of the leaflet's title, not a location given for the shots.
whyNot.3: No lobby is mentioned, and the library is used on weekdays.

A.q:
Read the passage.

The Arlo River runs 210 miles from the Brenner Hills to Lake Tuck. For most of its course it is shallow, with an average depth of 12 feet. Near the Carver Dam, however, the channel reaches 60 feet. The dam itself, completed in 1958, stands 45 feet tall.

According to the passage, how deep is the Arlo River near the Carver Dam?
A.why: The third sentence says that near the Carver Dam the channel reaches 60 feet.

whyNot.0: 12 feet is the average depth over most of the river.
whyNot.1: 45 feet is the height of the dam, not the depth of the river.
whyNot.3: 210 is the river's length in miles.

A.q: A student must find the year a state law was passed in a three-page article about the law's history. Which strategy is the most efficient?
options: Scan the article for a four-digit year
Skim the article for its general idea
Read the article closely from the start
Read the conclusion for the main claim
A.why: Looking for one specific detail calls for scanning: run your eyes over the text for a year, then read the sentence around it.

whyNot.1: Skimming gives the general idea, not a specific date.
whyNot.2: Close reading of all three pages is slow when one fact is needed.
whyNot.3: The conclusion states the main claim; the date may appear anywhere.

B.q: An article titled 'Choosing a Bike Helmet' has four headings: 'Sizing', 'Safety Certification', 'When to Replace' and 'Cleaning and Storage'. A reader wants to know whether a helmet should still be used after a minor fall. Under which heading should the reader look first?
B.why: Whether to keep using a helmet after a fall is a replacement question, so 'When to Replace' is the section most likely to hold it.

whyNot.0: Sizing covers fit, not damage after a fall.
whyNot.1: Certification covers the standards a new helmet meets, not when to stop using one.
whyNot.2: Cleaning and storage covers care, not whether a damaged helmet is still usable.

B.q:
Read the passage.

The Rosewood Clinic opened in 2012 with three exam rooms. In 2018, it moved to a larger building on Pine Street, where it had eleven exam rooms. In 2023, two of those rooms were converted into a laboratory. The clinic hired its first full-time pharmacist in 2020.

According to the passage, how many exam rooms does the clinic have now?
B.why: The clinic had eleven exam rooms after 2018, and in 2023 two became a laboratory: 11 − 2 = 9.

whyNot.0: Three was the number when the clinic opened in 2012.
whyNot.2: Eleven was the number before the 2023 conversion.
whyNot.3: This adds the two converted rooms instead of subtracting them.

B.q:
Read the passage.

Route 12 buses leave Central Station every 20 minutes from 6:00 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. on weekdays, then every 30 minutes until 7:00 p.m. On weekends, buses run every 45 minutes from 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.

How often do Route 12 buses leave Central Station at 11:00 a.m. on a Saturday?
B.why: Saturday is a weekend day, and weekend buses run every 45 minutes from 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., which includes 11:00 a.m.

whyNot.0: Every 20 minutes is the weekday morning rush schedule.
whyNot.2: Every 30 minutes is the weekday schedule after 9:00 a.m.

C.q:
Read the passage.

The Hartwell Nursing Program admits students twice a year. Applications for the fall class are due March 1, and applications for the spring class are due September 15. Every applicant must submit a TEAS score from the past two years. Applicants who earned a B or higher in anatomy and physiology receive priority. Interviews for the fall class are held in April; interviews for the spring class are held in October.

Jasmine is applying for the spring class. According to the passage, in which month are interviews for her class held?
C.why: The last sentence says interviews for the spring class are held in October.

whyNot.0: March 1 is the fall application deadline.
whyNot.1: April is when fall-class interviews are held.
whyNot.2: September 15 is the spring application deadline, not the interview month.

C.q:
Read the passage.

Volunteers at the Eastgate Food Bank sort donations on Tuesdays and pack boxes on Thursdays. Deliveries to homebound seniors go out every Friday morning. The warehouse is closed on weekends, but donations can be left in the bin by the side door.

On which day are food boxes brought to older residents who cannot leave their homes?
C.why: The question paraphrases 'homebound seniors'. The passage says deliveries to them go out every Friday morning.

whyNot.0: Tuesday is when donations are sorted.
whyNot.1: Thursday is when boxes are packed, the step before delivery.
whyNot.3: The warehouse is closed on weekends; only donations can be dropped off.

C.q:
Read the notice.

Bring unused or expired medicines to the Elm Street fire station on Saturday, May 10, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. Pills, patches and liquids are accepted; needles and inhalers are not. The service is free, and no questions are asked.

Which question can NOT be answered using the notice?
options: Is parking at the station free?
What time does the drop-off end?
Is there a charge for the service?
C.why: The notice says the service is free but says nothing about parking, so a parking fee cannot be determined from it.

whyNot.2: Answered: the drop-off runs until 2 p.m.

reteach.title: Finding a friend at a stadium
reteach.question: Your friend texts: 'Section 214, row K, seat 9.' You do not read every seat number in the stadium. What do you do instead, and how is that like a TEAS locate item?

blocks.body: You follow the signs to the 200 level (the heading), walk to Section 214 (the right paragraph), find row K (the sentence) and count to seat 9 (the exact detail). If you stop at row K in Section 241, you are in a real seat, just the wrong one: that is the 'real detail, wrong qualifier' trap. Scanning is that same narrowing search through a passage.

blocks.text: Section 241 has a row K and a seat 9 too. Check every part of the address, just as you check every qualifier in the question.

explain.body: Scanning searches for a specific word, number or name. Skimming reads lightly for the gist. For 'According to the passage, when/where/how many...?', scan.

test.q: Which task calls for scanning rather than skimming?
options: Getting a sense of what a long report covers
Finding the dose listed on a medicine label
Deciding whether an article is worth reading
Previewing a chapter's headings before class
test.why: Finding one specific fact, such as a dose, is a scanning task.

whyNot.0: A sense of what a report covers is the general idea, which calls for skimming.
whyNot.2: Judging whether an article is worth reading needs its general idea: skimming.
whyNot.3: Previewing headings is a skimming step for an overview.

explain.body: Headings and subheadings sort a text by topic. Match the question's topic to the heading, then scan only that section.

test.q: A handout has the headings 'Before Surgery', 'Day of Surgery' and 'Recovery at Home'. A patient wants to know what time to arrive at the hospital. Which section should he scan first?
test.why: Arrival time belongs to the day of the operation, so 'Day of Surgery' is the right section.

whyNot.0: 'Before Surgery' covers preparation in the days beforehand, such as eating and medicines.
whyNot.2: 'Recovery at Home' covers the period after surgery.
whyNot.3: A title names the topic; it does not hold specific details like arrival times.

explain.body: Questions often reword the passage. Scan for the idea as well as the exact word: 'physician' for 'doctor', 'yearly' for 'annual', 'older adults' for 'seniors'.

test.q:
Read the passage.

Members of the Westbrook Gym pay an annual fee of $240. Day passes cost $12, and a one-time key card costs $10.

How much does a membership cost per year?
test.why: 'Per year' matches 'annual', and the annual fee for members is $240.

whyNot.0: $10 is the one-time key card charge.
whyNot.1: $12 is the price of a day pass.
whyNot.3: This adds the other charges to the annual fee; the question asks for the membership cost per year.

explain.body: Qualifiers narrow the question: weekday or weekend, adult or child, before or after a change. The right answer matches the topic AND every qualifier.

test.q:
Read the passage.

Museum tickets cost $15 for adults and $8 for children ages 3 to 12. Children under 3 enter free. On Tuesdays after 6 p.m., admission is free for everyone.

How much will a family pay for one adult and a 5-year-old on a Tuesday at 2 p.m.?
test.why: 2 p.m. is before the free Tuesday evening hours, so normal prices apply: $15 for the adult plus $8 for a child aged 5 = $23.

whyNot.0: Free admission applies on Tuesdays after 6 p.m., not at 2 p.m.
whyNot.1: This counts the child's ticket but not the adult's.
whyNot.2: This counts the adult's ticket but not the child's; a 5-year-old is not under 3.
